claim: Fontfroide Abbey adult ticket prices range €14-€29 depending on visit type (self-guided, classic guided, Fayet tour, family treasure hunt), with family packages (2 adults + 2 children) at €42-€51 and children under 6 free; opening hours April-June and Sept-Oct 10:00-18:00, July-August 9:30-19:00.
quote: Children (6-25 years): €10-€19 depending on visit type; Adults: €14-€29 depending on visit type; Family packages (2 adults + 2 children): €42-€51. April-June 10:00-18:00, July-August 9:30-19:00, September-October 10:00-18:00.

claim: Fontfroide Abbey was rescued in 1908 by painter Gustave Fayet and his wife Madeleine, remains privately owned by the Fayet heirs, and combines a Cistercian monastery with a working AOC Corbières wine estate, restaurant 'La Table de Fontfroide', and stained glass windows commissioned by Fayet in the 1920s.
quote: French painter Gustave Fayet and his wife Madeleine rescued the abbey in 1908 after it was abandoned. It is still privately owned and the family has continued to restore the 12-century abbey. The abbey produces AOC Corbières wines.

claim: Fontfroide is classified as a national heritage site since 1843, the second most visited site in Occitanie, and operates 40+ hectares of vineyards producing AOC Corbières wines exported across the region.
quote: In 1908, Gustave Fayet, a local winemaker, bought the site... The abbey has more than 40 hectares of vineyards and its own restaurant... AOC Corbières wines are produced at the abbey.

claim: Fontfroide is described as one of the most remarkably preserved Cistercian ensembles in Europe, featuring pink stone, a majestic cloister, 8 hectares of parks and gardens, and a rose garden of around 2,500 roses across 14 varieties admirable from April to September.
quote: one of the most remarkably preserved Cistercian ensembles in Europe... pink stone, a majestic cloister, remarkable gardens and a preserved massif... 1,000 years of history across 8 hectares of parks and gardens.

claim: Lagrasse is officially classified as one of 'Les Plus Beaux Villages de France', a medieval village in the Corbières valley along the Orbieu river with cobbled streets, a 14th-century covered market hall, fortified Pont Vieux, and the famous Benedictine abbey founded in 779 under Charlemagne.
quote: Lagrasse, l'un des Plus Beaux Villages de France... ruelles pavées, sa halle couverte, son vieux pont, sa célèbre abbaye.

claim: The Abbey of Lagrasse is uniquely split into two distinct ownerships: a 'small' medieval public part owned by the Aude department since 2004 (open for paid visits including dormitory, chapels, abbatial palace) and a 'great part' inhabited since 2004 by the Regular Canons of the Mother of God living under the rule of Saint Augustine.
quote: The abbey today is composed of two distinct parts: a public part belonging to the Aude department and a private part inhabited by a community of canons... the 'great part' was returned to religious life in 2004 with the purchase by the community of the Regular Canons of the Mother of God.

claim: The 31st Banquet du Livre d'Été literary festival runs at the public Abbaye de Lagrasse from 25-31 July 2026 on the theme 'La maison et le monde', with announced guests including Patrick Boucheron, Bénédicte Savoy, Tanguy Viel and Mohamed El Kathib; the abbey also hosts a Spring and Autumn Banquet, plus 'En blanc et noir' piano festival.
quote: Banquet du livre d'été 2026 : La maison et le monde... du 25 au 31 juillet... guests include Patrick Boucheron, Bénédicte Savoy, Tanguy Viel, and Mohamed El Kathib.

claim: Lagrasse is celebrated for its independent artisan craft shops lining the cobblestone streets, the Saturday morning market in the 14th-century halle, a literary bistro and the bookstore 'Les arts de lire' operating within the abbey complex.
quote: narrow, winding cobblestone streets lead visitors through historic buildings, with many streets lined with independent craft shops showcasing local artisans and their unique creations.

claim: Château de Villerouge-Termenès charges €7 adults / €3 children, opening daily 10:00-19:30 in July-August and Mon-Fri 10-13h & 14-18h plus weekends 10-18h non-stop from April-June and September-November; closed mid-December to March.
quote: Adults: €7, Children: €3... July 1 - August 31: Daily: 10am-7:30pm... April 1 - June 30 & Sept 1 - Nov 1: Mon-Fri: 10am-1pm, 2pm-6pm | Sat-Sun: 10am-6pm.

claim: Villerouge-Termenès castle, built XII-XIV centuries by the Archbishops of Narbonne, is famous as the site where Guilhem Bélibaste — the last known Cathar parfait — was burnt alive in 1321 on the archbishop's orders; the castle is an irregular pentagon with round towers and now hosts an audio-visual exhibit on Catharism plus the 'Medieval Rôtisserie' restaurant serving 14th-century cuisine, unique in Europe.
quote: It was here that the last known Cathar parfait, Guilhem Belibaste, was burnt alive in 1321... the 'Medieval Rotisserie', a restaurant offering 14th century cuisine unique in Europe.

claim: A 'Pass des incontournables Corbières-Minervois' at €15 gives reduced-rate access to three partner sites — the public Abbey of Lagrasse, Château de Termes, and Château de Villerouge-Termenès — making it efficient to combine all three on day trips.
quote: Pass des incontournables Corbières-Minervois available for 15€, which includes reduced-rate access to three partner sites: the Abbey of Lagrasse (public section), Château de Termes, and Château de Villerouge-Termenès.

claim: Bages is a perched fishing village on a rocky outcrop above the 5,000-hectare Bages-Sigean lagoon (largest on the Côte du Midi), home to artists drawn by the light, with three art galleries (L'étang d'art, Latuvu, La Maison des Arts), daily fresh-fish landings 10:30-12:00, and eel as the local culinary specialty.
quote: occupies a distinctive rocky outcrop perched above the Bages-Sigean lagoon... has attracted numerous artists drawn by the exceptional light... Three art galleries operate in Bages: L'étang d'art, Latuvu, La Maison des Arts.

claim: The Étang de Bages-Sigean lagoon hosts roughly 5,000 pink flamingos and 350+ bird species, with signposted hiking and cycling loops departing from Bages, Peyriac-de-Mer and Sigean inside the Narbonnaise en Méditerranée Regional Natural Park.
quote: There would be 5,000 flamingos in this area. An extraordinary assortment of birds (350 species have been spotted here)... long-distance hiking trails offering several signposted itineraries.

claim: Driving distances from Fontjoncouse: Fontfroide Abbey ~13 km, Lagrasse ~14-29 km (≈44 min via roads), Villerouge-Termenès within 30 km via the D613/D40, making all three viable as single-stop day trips from the Auberge du Vieux Puits.
quote: Fontfroide Abbey is at 13 km from Fontjoncouse, and Lagrasse is at 14 km... drive from Lagrasse to Fontjoncouse takes 44 minutes for a distance of 28.9 kilometers.
